sources: Offset pagination: 1-based page to offset mapping (off-by-one on page index)
Keyset/stable ordering: ORDER BY with unique tie-breaker column for deterministic paging
Server-side page size clamp applied at every public entry point

defects.description: page_offset(1, 25) returns 25, so page 1 skips the first 25 rows; page 2 returns rows 51-75 and rows 26-50 are never returned. Expected offset is (page - 1) * size (R2).

export_all(conn, 'u1', 1, 500, start, end) passes size=500 unclamped to repo.fetch_page (repo does no clamp), so up to 500 rows are returned in one call, violating R1 (never above 100). list_records clamps, export_all does not.
Three records share created_at T. With size=2: page 1 may return A,B and page 2 may return B,C (or A,C), so rows repeat or are skipped across pages. ORDER BY must include id DESC (R3).

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Caps every size above 100 at 100; sizes below 1 and None are handled before this line, so this is the correct clamp (R1).
Half-open window with bound parameters, matching R4. Parameters are the UTC-normalised datetimes from api._utc.
The count query has no LIMIT on purpose. R5 requires the total of matching rows, not of the page, so ignoring paging is correct here.
Rejects naive datetimes before conversion, which is the rule in R4; aware datetimes are converted to UTC by astimezone.

Unchanged line in this change (exists in base/api.py). Whitespace-only user_id passes the presence check and is stored as an empty string in the audit entry, a real weakness on an untouched line; it is outside the seeded change and a diff-mode reviewer must not report it.

accepted_extras.note: export_all never applies the default page size, size None reaches page * size
